title: spec(ui): `record:details` / `record:highlights` / `record:related_list` declare `enforceFieldSecurity` and `redactFields` — `requiredPermissions` forks on a measured fail-open gate
body:
Part of #18159

Clause-②: yes (widening)

⚠️ **`Part of`, not a closing keyword, and deliberately so.** The card routes three keys here and asks for a per-key exit. Two are declared below. The third, `requiredPermissions`, returns a **fork** that only a ruling can settle — merging this PR must not close the card, because the half it leaves open is the half with a measured fail-open gate behind it.

---

## What this declares

`record:details`, `record:highlights` and `record:related_list` are `strictObject`s that declared neither `enforceFieldSecurity` nor `redactFields`, while `@object-ui/plugin-detail` reads and honours both on each of the three. An author who wrote either was refused at publish and the same document was honoured on the raw-node path. Both keys are now declared on all three blocks — optional, no schema default, so an absent key stays absent rather than becoming "the author asked for off".

| key | what the render path does |
|:---|:---|
| `enforceFieldSecurity` (boolean) | Folds the block's field list — the detail body's `fields` and `sections`, the highlight chips, the related list's `columns` — through the caller's field-read permissions (`checkField`, the platform's own answer) before rendering. |
| `redactFields` (string array) | Drops the names it lists outright. On `record:related_list` it is also handed down to `RelatedList`, because that component derives its own columns when none are authored — filtering the authored array alone let a redacted field return through the derivation (objectui#9053). |

**The claim is held to what the render path does.** Both are presentation filters applied in the browser after the record is fetched: the values are in the page either way, so neither is a data-access control and neither is the object's `publicSharing.redactFields`, which removes them server-side. Each `describe()` says that in the text an author reads, rather than leaving the key names to imply it (Prime Directive #10). The gates that do keep a value from a caller are the field's own `requiredPermissions` / `maskingRule` (ADR-0066 D3) and the permission set.

## What this deliberately does NOT declare — `requiredPermissions` forks

The card's Zone 3 instruction was to stop rather than declare a key whose honouring is itself the defect. That condition is met for `requiredPermissions`, and it is met on a measurement, not a reading of intent.

The renderers evaluate it as `perms.can(objectName, name)` (`record-details.tsx`, `record-highlights.tsx`, `record-related-list.tsx`, each writing `name as any`). That second parameter is typed `PermissionAction` — **this package's own closed enum**, `packages/spec/src/kernel/plugin-security-advanced.zod.ts`: `create` · `read` · `update` · `delete` · `execute` · `manage` · `configure` · `share` · `export` · `import` · `admin`. It is not the ADR-0066 capability set, which is what `requiredPermissions` means on `action`, `app`, `field` and `bulkAction`, and which objectui evaluates through a different function entirely (`hasCapabilities`, over `systemPermissions`).

Both shipped providers were run, each with self-tests and controls that fire in both directions:

**`MePermissionsProvider`** (the backend-backed one, `/me/permissions`). Its `check` maps eight spellings to a permission bit and falls through: `const k = map[action as string] ?? 'allowRead'`. Driven with `allowRead: true`, every write bit `false`, and `systemPermissions: []` — reported, holding nothing:

```
SELFTEST ok     granted verb 'read' -> allowed
SELFTEST ok     ungranted verb 'delete' -> denied
  can('contract', "read"                     ) -> true
  can('contract', "create"                   ) -> false
  can('contract', "delete"                   ) -> false
  can('contract', "manage"                   ) -> true     -- in the enum, NOT in the map
  can('contract', "admin"                    ) -> true     -- in the enum, NOT in the map
  can('contract', "crm.manage"               ) -> true     -- a capability nobody holds
  can('contract', "showcase.restricted_ops"  ) -> true     -- a capability nobody holds
```

**`PermissionProvider`** (the role-based one), through its real `evaluatePermission`:

```
SELFTEST ok     granted verb 'read' with a config present -> allowed
SELFTEST ok     ungranted verb 'delete' with a config present -> denied
SELFTEST ok     no config for the object at all -> allowed (documented default)
  config PRESENT  can('contract', "crm.manage"  ) -> false   -- denied for EVERYONE
  config ABSENT   can('contract', "crm.manage"  ) -> true    -- allowed for EVERYONE
```

So one authored `requiredPermissions: ['crm.manage']` passes for every reader who can read the object under one provider, is denied to every reader under the other, and consults the caller's actual capability set under neither. Declaring it would mint the ADR-0049 **fail-open access gate** this repo retired from `app.areas[].requiredPermissions` in 17.0.0 — whose own conversion-registry entry says it in the same words: *"FAIL-OPEN access gates: no layer ever read them, so a 'hidden' or permission-gated area was served and rendered to every user"*.

⭐ objectui's own pin battery for this gate (`record-quick-actions.requiredPermissions-gate.test.tsx`) **mocks `usePermissions`** with a stub whose `can(object, action)` is `granted.has(action)`. It pins that the renderer calls `can()` with the right arguments; it cannot see what `can()` answers, which is where the defect lives.

**The question for the seat** is in the report on the card. In short: (A) declare it as object ACTIONS (`PermissionActionSchema`), which is what `record-highlights.tsx`'s own comment says the author should write — *"record:\* may declare requiredPermissions like ['read','update']"* — and what the backend-backed provider's map can honour; (B) declare it as ADR-0066 capabilities and repair the renderer to evaluate it through `hasCapabilities`; (C) rule it host-composition surface and retire the reads, the ADR-0049 precedent. ⛔ Not decided here.

## Also measured, and left alone

`record:quick_actions` **already declares** `requiredPermissions` (`z.array(z.string())`, described as *"unless the current user holds every named permission on this object"*) and its renderer performs the identical `perms.can(objectName, p as any)` read. That declaration is on a published surface and predates this branch; it is not touched here and is reported for filing rather than fixed on a card that does not name it.

## Evidence

One instrument, self-tested before it was pointed at the tree, run on the same tree before and after the change. Two positive controls, both unmoved:

```
                        BEFORE                            AFTER
ComponentPropsMap       48 entries                        48 entries
strict blocks           47 (loose: user:profile)          47 (loose: user:profile)
requiredPermissions     A=1 [record:quick_actions]        A=1 [record:quick_actions]
enforceFieldSecurity    A=0 []                            A=3 [details, related_list, highlights]
redactFields            A=0 []                            A=3 [details, related_list, highlights]
aria   POSITIVE CONTROL A=21                              A=21
fields POSITIVE CONTROL A=7                               A=7
```

Named refusals on `record:related_list`, base document legal on its own:

```
                                 BEFORE                                  AFTER
CONTROL+  +columns               success=true                            success=true
CONTROL-  +zzqx_no_such_key      success=false  unrecognized_keys [...]  success=false  unrecognized_keys [...]
          +requiredPermissions   success=false  unrecognized_keys [...]  success=false  unrecognized_keys [...]
          +enforceFieldSecurity  success=false  unrecognized_keys [...]  success=true
          +redactFields          success=false  unrecognized_keys [...]  success=true
          baseline               success=true                            success=true
```

`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json` moved by exactly six lines, all additions, and nothing else.

## Verification

Run on `676d44d593`, the head this PR carries.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/ui/component-record-block-field-security.test.ts` — 18 tests, exit 0. With the three sibling component suites: 4 files / 397 tests, exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` — exit 0 (test layer: 54 files / 259 errors / 144 pinned signatures held, unmoved).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` — exit 0. `gen:api-surface-declarations` and `gen:docs` were regenerated after the check proved them stale; `authorable-surface/ui.json` is the build's own output. `authorable-surface.base.json` is untouched.
- `MANIFEST=$PWD/sdui.manifest.json pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:react-declaration-parity --baseline react-declaration-parity.baseline.json --strict` — exit 0, as `lint.yml` spells it. ⚠️ Note this gate does not cover these three blocks at all: they are withdrawn from the react tier (`REACT_RECORD_BLOCK_ALTERNATIVES`), so no `spec-only` signal arises here — and `spec-only` is a reported, never-ratcheted signal in any case.
- `pnpm lint` — the whole tree, `eslint . --no-inline-config`, exit 0. No narrowing was needed.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ran RECORD_FILE` — **107 derived families accounted for: 106 run, 1 NOT MEASURED.** The one is `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, which exits 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`) because ~34 packages have no `dist/` in this worktree; it needs a whole-workspace build, which CI's `Build Core` provides. Six other families first exited 3 or 1 on the same prerequisite class and were re-run green after building `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/client-react` and `@objectstack/driver-turso`.

## Acceptance notes

Out of scope for this card, noted and not filed from here:

- **`record:quick_actions.requiredPermissions` carries the same defect on a published surface** (`z.array(z.string())`, described as a capability gate, evaluated against the closed action enum). Reported for filing; deliberately not fixed on a card that does not name it. Successor: the same ruling that settles this card's fork.
- **`redactFields` neighbours `hideFields` on `record:details`**, and on a well-formed field list the two remove the same rows. They are different channels — `hideFields` is the dedupe list the renderer also writes to (live `record:highlights` registrations, the page-title field), `redactFields` is the author's deliberate omission and the arm that participates in the fail-closed fold — and the TSDoc says so. Converging them is a contract question this card did not open. Successor: whoever next edits `RecordDetailsProps`.
- **`packages/spec/src/ui/react-blocks.ts` was in the dispatched file surface and needed no edit.** All three blocks are withdrawn from the react tier because they take their record from context, so they carry `REACT_RECORD_BLOCK_ALTERNATIVES` rows rather than published props. Carrier: none — stated so the absence reads as measured rather than skipped.

## ⚠️ Not measured

- The runtime behaviour of either declared key in a browser. No dogfood or integration run was made for this change, by anyone on this chain.
- Whether any authored document anywhere writes these keys. "The schema refused it" is not "nobody writes it"; only the first is measured.
- Whether the same gap exists on element faces beyond these three blocks. The census above covers all 48 `ComponentPropsMap` entries for the three key names; the renderer side was read only for `@object-ui/plugin-detail`.
